_readme: AN INVENTED FORM, in the shape `node src/forms/inspect_ats_form.mjs --options` writes: the drafter's input.
It exists so the end-to-end test can drive `src/forms/draft_form_spec.py` with no browser, no network and
no flakiness, and it is deliberately a form only THIS configuration can answer: identity and contact from
the two profiles, one question answered by the `answer_rules.json` the bootstrap wrote, one question no
profile can answer (the College of Nurses registration NUMBER) that must therefore come back as a gap
rather than as a guess, and a LinkedIn field — which this person does not have, so the example person's
LinkedIn URL must not appear there or anywhere else in the drafted spec.
The refs use the scanner's own conventions (`id:` / `name:` / `group:`), because the drafter falls back to
them when a label matches nothing: `id:city` and `id:postal_code` are what answer an ordinary text input
whose question is only a word. `react_select: true` is what the scanner reports for a control whose class
or role says select — the two structured questions here are that shape, so they are answered with the
form's own option text instead of a bare string.

fields.label: College of Nurses of Ontario registration number
Have you previously been employed by Toronto General Hospital?
